{"analyses":[{"paper_id":"2606.15906","title":"MAGE-RAG: Multigranular Adaptive Graph Evidence for Agentic Multimodal RAG in Long-Document QA","research_question":"Can long-document multimodal question answering improve evidence coverage and control irrelevant context by dynamically constructing a query-specific page-and-element evidence subgraph under explicit budgets instead of relying on fixed top-k retrieval?","methodology":"MAGE-RAG first converts each static document into a heterogeneous evidence graph containing page nodes and fine-grained element nodes such as paragraphs, tables, figures, charts, formulas, and code, connected by containment, reading-order, layout, section, and semantic-neighbor relations. At query time, an agentic controller retrieves initial pages and iteratively opens, searches, expands, and prunes graph evidence under resource budgets. A structured renderer then supplies selected page images, local element images or crops, text, and node references to a multimodal reader. The framework is evaluated on LongDocURL and MMLongBench-Doc, with ablations of page retrieval, node rendering, graph expansion, and controller behavior.","key_findings":[{"finding":"MAGE-RAG reports 52.75 overall accuracy on LongDocURL and 53.26 accuracy with 51.19 F1 on MMLongBench-Doc, showing that dynamically assembled graph evidence can be competitive with strong long-document multimodal QA baselines.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§4 Experiments, main results"},{"finding":"The framework shows particularly large gains on cross-page questions in MMLongBench-Doc, where its reported cross-page score is 34.70 compared with 24.87 for M3DocRAG and 24.51 for EVisRAG.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§4 Experiments, main results"},{"finding":"Ablations show that fine-grained node rendering and graph-neighbor expansion improve performance over page-only retrieval; graph-neighbor expansion raises the reported MMLongBench-Doc accuracy/F1 to 53.88/50.20 from 48.75/45.71 for the top-k page-only configuration.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§4 Ablation Study"},{"finding":"The evidence representation preserves within-document provenance through page identifiers, element nodes, bounding boxes, image references, and page-node alignment, allowing the final reader input and controller trajectory to be inspected at multiple granularities.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§3 Method and §4 Analysis"},{"finding":"The paper explicitly identifies offline parsing and evidence-graph quality as an upper bound on the system and notes that the controller adds evaluator calls and state-management cost, making the approach less compelling for short or simple single-hop documents.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§5 Conclusion"}],"limitations":["The method operates on a single static document representation and does not define persistent element or region identities across successive revisions of the same attachment.","Page, node, bounding-box, and image references are useful within one parsed document but are not revision-stable lineage identifiers.","The quality ceiling depends on the offline parser, element segmentation, captions, OCR, and graph construction.","The online controller requires additional model calls and state management compared with fixed retrieval.","The authors note that the approach may not be cost-effective for short or simple single-hop documents.","Performance gains are not uniform across every benchmark slice or comparison, so the reported aggregate gains should not be interpreted as universal superiority."],"reproducibility":{"code_available":true,"dataset_available":true,"metrics_reported":true},"confidence_scores":{"overall_benchmark_performance":0.99,"cross_page_gain":0.99,"graph_ablation_gain":0.99,"within_document_provenance":0.97,"static_document_only":0.96,"parser_and_controller_limits":0.99},"raw_claims":["MAGE-RAG represents long multimodal documents as graphs containing both page-level and element-level evidence.","Element nodes can carry textual content, structured content, bounding boxes, semantic types, and optional image references.","Edges encode structural and semantic relationships including containment, reading order, layout adjacency, section hierarchy, and semantic neighborhood.","The query-time controller can open, search, expand, and prune evidence rather than consuming a fixed retrieval set.","The renderer aligns selected textual evidence and visual crops with page and node references before answer generation.","Graph-neighbor expansion improves the reported QA results relative to page-only retrieval in the ablation study.","The controller trajectory records actions and retained evidence, providing an auditable retrieval trace.","The framework's performance depends on the quality of the document parser and the evidence graph constructed before querying.","The paper does not introduce a mechanism for matching the same visual region or logical element across revised versions of a document."],"source_url":"https://arxiv.org/html/2606.15906","access":"full_text"},{"paper_id":"2605.12882","title":"CiteVQA: Benchmarking Evidence Attribution for Trustworthy Document Intelligence","research_question":"How can document visual question answering be evaluated so that a model receives credit only when its answer is correct and its cited document region genuinely supports that answer?","methodology":"CiteVQA constructs a benchmark of 1,897 questions over 711 PDFs spanning seven domains and two languages, including single-document and multi-document settings. Its automated construction pipeline parses documents, links related documents, extracts evidence packages, generates and verifies question-answer pairs, and uses masking ablation to identify crucial evidence before expert review. Gold evidence is represented at element-level bounding-box granularity with document and page indices, and synthetic multi-document evidence is mapped back to coordinates in the original source PDFs. Twenty multimodal language models are evaluated using evidence recall, relevance, answer correctness, page-level metrics, and Strict Attributed Accuracy, which jointly requires acceptable answers and evidence.","key_findings":[{"finding":"CiteVQA demonstrates a substantial gap between answer correctness and faithful evidence attribution: the strongest evaluated system reports 76.0 Strict Attributed Accuracy despite an 86.1 answer score, while the strongest open-source model reports 22.5 SAA.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"Abstract and §4 Main Results"},{"finding":"Evidence attribution becomes more difficult as document scope increases; for the strongest system, reported evidence recall decreases from 68.9 in the single-document setting to 55.3 in the multi-document multiple-gold setting.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§4 Main Results and Appendix analysis of multi-document complexity"},{"finding":"Restricting models to ground-truth pages or gold documents improves answer accuracy in the paper's oracle-style analyses, providing preliminary evidence that evidence localization is itself an important performance bottleneck rather than merely an explanation layer.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§5.2 Further Analysis of Evidence Attribution"},{"finding":"The benchmark provides a hierarchical spatial evidence address consisting of document index, page index, and element bounding box, and its multi-document synthesis pipeline maintains a mapping from synthetic evidence back to source-PDF coordinates.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§4.1 Evaluation Metrics and §8.1 Spatial Mapping and Evidence Synthesis"},{"finding":"A human study on a sampled subset finds no statistically significant difference between the automated and human assessments for the reported relevance and answer-correctness judging dimensions, supporting the evaluation pipeline's use of automated judges.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§9.2 Validation of Automated Evaluation via Human Study"}],"limitations":["CiteVQA grounds evidence in static PDF coordinates and does not define stable region identifiers or lineage across successive revisions of the same PDF.","Document index, page index, and bounding-box coordinates can change after pagination, layout, or content revisions, so they are not by themselves revision-stable identifiers.","The automated annotation pipeline relies on capable document parsers and MLLMs and is computationally expensive to reproduce at full scale.","The paper notes that determining authoritative evidence can be domain-dependent even when a visually matching region is available.","Evaluation uses model-based relevance and correctness judges, adding cost and another possible source of error despite the reported human validation.","The benchmark distribution may encourage overfitting if systems are tuned closely to its domains and document characteristics.","Benchmark annotations and code are available, but access to the complete source-PDF collection is constrained by copyright and may require approval or rely on external URLs."],"reproducibility":{"code_available":true,"dataset_available":true,"metrics_reported":true},"confidence_scores":{"answer_attribution_gap":1.0,"multi_document_difficulty":0.99,"localization_bottleneck":0.94,"hierarchical_bbox_provenance":1.0,"judge_validation":0.98,"no_cross_version_lineage":0.97},"raw_claims":["CiteVQA contains 1,897 questions derived from 711 multi-page PDFs across seven broad domains and two languages.","Each gold citation identifies evidence at element-level bounding-box granularity rather than only at page level.","Strict Attributed Accuracy requires both the answer and the supporting evidence to satisfy the benchmark's correctness criteria.","Models can produce correct textual answers while citing incorrect document regions.","The benchmark includes single-document, multi-document one-gold, and multi-document multiple-gold scenarios.","Masking candidate evidence elements is used during dataset construction to help identify evidence that is crucial for answering a question.","Synthetic multi-document evidence is mapped back to the spatial coordinates of its original source document.","The released repository contains inference, evaluation, summarization, prompts, and benchmark-data tooling.","Oracle-style restriction to correct pages or documents improves answer accuracy for several evaluated models.","CiteVQA does not track the identity of a document element across revised versions of the same attachment."],"source_url":"https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12882","access":"full_text"},{"paper_id":"2601.08741","title":"From Rows to Reasoning: A Retrieval-Augmented Multimodal Framework for Spreadsheet Understanding","research_question":"Can a retrieval-first multimodal architecture reason accurately and audibly over large multi-sheet spreadsheets by indexing and retrieving fine-grained spreadsheet evidence instead of placing an entire workbook into the model context?","methodology":"The framework, FRTR, decomposes workbooks into multiple retrieval units including rows, columns, sliding windows, and embedded images, then serializes and embeds those units for hybrid lexical and dense retrieval. Reciprocal Rank Fusion combines lexical and semantic rankings, after which the selected spreadsheet units and associated metadata are supplied to an LLM that returns an answer and reasoning information. The authors introduce FRTR-Bench, consisting of 30 synthetic enterprise-style Excel workbooks with large tables, multiple sheets, cross-sheet formulas, and embedded images, and questions annotated with explicit provenance such as cells, formulas, or image identifiers. Experiments compare FRTR with SpreadsheetLLM and full-context baselines and include retrieval-method and indexing-granularity ablations.","key_findings":[{"finding":"On FRTR-Bench, hybrid Reciprocal Rank Fusion retrieval reaches 0.74 answer accuracy compared with 0.59 for vector-only retrieval and 0.42 for lexical-only retrieval.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§5.3.1 Retrieval Method Ablation"},{"finding":"Combining row, column, window, and image retrieval units reaches 0.74 accuracy, compared with 0.52 for rows only, 0.18 for columns only, and 0.58 for windows only, supporting the value of multi-granular spreadsheet indexing.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§5.3.2 Unit Granularity Ablation"},{"finding":"On FRTR-Bench, the reported FRTR configuration reaches 0.74 accuracy while the paper's SpreadsheetLLM comparison reaches 0.24, although this comparison reflects the authors' adaptation and benchmark setup rather than SpreadsheetLLM's own original benchmark conditions.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§5.1 and §5.3"},{"finding":"On the SpreadsheetLLM benchmark, FRTR is competitive but does not exceed SpreadsheetLLM in raw accuracy for the strongest models; for example, the reported GPT-5 results are 0.87 for FRTR and 0.90 for SpreadsheetLLM.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§5.2 SpreadsheetLLM Benchmark Evaluation"},{"finding":"The benchmark and retrieval pipeline retain explicit within-workbook provenance through sheet locations, cell references, formulas, and image identifiers, but this provenance addresses a particular workbook state rather than lineage across workbook revisions.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§4 FRTR-Bench and §5 Discussion"}],"limitations":["FRTR-Bench contains synthetic enterprise-style workbooks rather than naturally evolving production workbooks.","The benchmark is English-only.","The benchmark contains 30 workbooks and 157 questions, limiting the diversity of revision patterns and real organizational spreadsheet practices it can represent.","The system generates formulas and cell references but does not execute formulas or modify workbooks.","Initial workbook indexing has a one-time cost even though subsequent retrieval is reported to be fast.","Image-dependent question accuracy is reported at 65%, leaving substantial multimodal headroom.","Sheet names, A1-style cell addresses, and image identifiers provide provenance inside one workbook version but do not establish stable identities when rows, columns, sheets, formulas, or images are inserted, deleted, moved, or renamed.","The paper does not model revised-workbook provenance or correspondences between elements in successive workbook versions."],"reproducibility":{"code_available":false,"dataset_available":true,"metrics_reported":true},"confidence_scores":{"hybrid_retrieval_ablation":1.0,"multigranular_ablation":1.0,"frtr_bench_gain":0.99,"spreadsheetllm_parity_nuance":1.0,"within_workbook_provenance":0.97,"no_revision_lineage":0.98},"raw_claims":["FRTR indexes spreadsheet rows, columns, localized windows, and embedded images as separate retrieval units.","The retrieval stage combines lexical and dense rankings using Reciprocal Rank Fusion.","FRTR-Bench contains 30 synthetic enterprise-style workbooks with 155 sheets and more than 3.9 million cells.","Benchmark questions include provenance annotations that can identify supporting cells, formulas, or images.","Hybrid retrieval outperforms either dense-only or lexical-only retrieval in the reported ablation.","Using all indexing granularities outperforms each single-granularity alternative in the reported ablation.","FRTR is roughly comparable to SpreadsheetLLM on SpreadsheetLLM's own benchmark but has lower raw accuracy for several high-capacity models.","The framework retrieves evidence rather than compressing an entire workbook into one context.","The paper reports 65% accuracy on image-dependent FRTR-Bench questions.","The framework does not provide persistent spreadsheet-element identities across different revisions of a workbook."],"source_url":"https://arxiv.org/html/2601.08741","access":"full_text"},{"paper_id":"2607.29638","title":"HierDoc: Hierarchical Page-to-Region Evidence Routing for Long-Document Visual Question Answering","research_question":"Can long-document visual question answering improve evidence acquisition by learning page selection and fine-grained region selection as successive hierarchical policies rather than retrieving only pages or treating page and region evidence independently?","methodology":"HierDoc implements a two-stage evidence-routing pipeline in which a page policy first selects relevant physical pages and a region policy then chooses parsed regions only from those pages. MinerU2.5 produces candidate regions represented by a sample-local action alias, physical page index, bounding box, semantic type, and OCR or table content. The selectors are trained stage-wise with Group Relative Policy Optimization and can invoke bounded reflection, while the answer model receives selected full pages together with selected region crops and associated text. The system is evaluated on five long-document and table-oriented visual QA benchmarks with retrieval and QA ablations.","key_findings":[{"finding":"The Qwen3-VL-based HierDoc configuration reports 53.62 on MMLongBench-Doc and 65.80 on LongDocURL, alongside competitive results on SlideVQA, PaperTab, and FetaTab.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§4 Main Results"},{"finding":"Adding the learned region-routing stage to the page-only configuration improves the reported MMLongBench-Doc result from 50.8 accuracy and 45.6 F1 to 53.6 accuracy and 47.8 F1 when GRPO and reflection are used.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§4 Ablation Study"},{"finding":"Training the page selector with GRPO and adding reflection improves page-routing quality and downstream QA relative to the untrained selector in the reported ablation.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§4 Ablation Study"},{"finding":"Selected visual crops plus selected OCR provide stronger gains than indiscriminately adding all OCR, while removing the full selected pages and retaining only local crops and OCR reduces performance, showing that global page context and local region evidence are complementary.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§4 Evidence Composition Analysis"},{"finding":"HierDoc carries hierarchical within-document evidence metadata from physical page to parsed region and bounding box, but its region aliases are sample-local action identifiers rather than persistent identities designed to survive document revisions.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§3 Method"}],"limitations":["The region stage can only inspect pages retained by the first stage, so page-routing mistakes can cause irreversible evidence loss.","Region quality depends on MinerU parsing, OCR, table parsing, and spatial alignment.","Page and region selectors are optimized stage-wise rather than jointly from end-to-end answer feedback.","The evidence representation is designed for a static document instance and contains no version identifier or cross-version lineage mechanism.","Region aliases are sample-local and bounding boxes are tied to the current page geometry, so neither is a stable identifier after document revision.","The paper does not address message-to-attachment referring expressions or correspondence between revised attachments."],"reproducibility":{"code_available":false,"dataset_available":true,"metrics_reported":true},"confidence_scores":{"main_benchmark_results":0.99,"region_stage_gain":1.0,"page_policy_training_gain":0.99,"global_local_complementarity":0.99,"hierarchical_region_metadata":0.99,"no_cross_version_identity":0.97},"raw_claims":["HierDoc first selects relevant pages and then selects finer regions only within those pages.","Candidate regions carry a physical page index, bounding box, semantic type, and extracted textual content.","The page and region policies are trained using stage-wise reinforcement-learning objectives.","Bounded reflection allows a selector to reconsider an evidence set under specified conditions.","The final answer model consumes both complete selected pages and finer selected evidence regions.","Learned region selection improves the reported QA result over page-only evidence.","Selected crops and OCR are more useful than simply adding all parsed OCR in the reported evidence-composition study.","Retaining global selected-page context remains beneficial even when fine-grained region crops are available.","Errors made by the first-stage page router can prevent the correct region from ever being considered.","The system does not assign a persistent region identity that follows an element through successive document versions."],"source_url":"https://arxiv.org/html/2607.29638","access":"full_text"},{"paper_id":"manual-ae200642f8","title":"Change-Centric Management of Versions in an XML Warehouse","research_question":"How can an XML warehouse represent and store document version histories so that node identity persists across snapshots, changes can be composed or reversed, and new versions can be installed efficiently?","methodology":"The paper treats a document history as a sequence of XML snapshots and applies an XML diff algorithm between consecutive snapshots to identify corresponding nodes and assign persistent XML identifiers, or XIDs. Rather than retaining only lossy simple deltas, it introduces completed deltas containing sufficient information to support both forward and backward application as well as delta composition. The proposed physical organization stores the current version, an XID mapping, and a history of completed deltas, emphasizing append-oriented installation of new versions. The authors implemented the techniques in the Xyleme/Natix environment and evaluated storage behavior using simulated XML changes at varying modification rates.","key_findings":[{"finding":"Persistent XIDs give corresponding XML nodes a continuing logical identity across document snapshots, directly addressing the problem of referring to the same element through multiple versions.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§3 Identifying Nodes Across Versions"},{"finding":"Completed deltas retain information omitted by simple deltas and can therefore be inverted and composed, allowing navigation and transformation across a version history.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§2 Version Management and completed-delta definitions"},{"finding":"A document history can be represented by the latest materialized version together with a sequence of completed deltas, from which earlier states can be reconstructed by applying changes backward.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"§2 Version Management and storage representation"},{"finding":"The proposed physical layout makes installation of a newly acquired version largely append-oriented, reducing updates to previously stored objects at the cost of redundant information in completed deltas.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"Storage policy and implementation discussion"},{"finding":"Simulation experiments show that delta-storage cost grows with the amount of modification and that richer completed deltas consume more space than simpler change representations, motivating compression and storage-policy optimization.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"Experimental Results and Conclusion"}],"limitations":["The storage experiments rely on simulated document changes rather than a released corpus of naturally evolving web documents.","The authors state that the influence of XML document structure on storage behavior was not fully studied.","Warehouse acquisition snapshots may miss intervening real-world edits, and the recorded version time is acquisition time rather than necessarily the true update time.","Persistent identity depends on the diff algorithm correctly deciding which nodes in different snapshots correspond to one another.","The model addresses logical XML-tree nodes, not multimodal page regions, rendered bounding boxes, spreadsheet cells, or visual elements.","The paper predates modern document QA and does not connect node lineage to answer-span evidence identifiers or natural-language referring expressions.","Some formal proofs and detailed algorithms are omitted from the paper for space reasons.","The implementation is described but no public source-code release or experimental dataset is provided."],"reproducibility":{"code_available":false,"dataset_available":false,"metrics_reported":true},"confidence_scores":{"persistent_xid_lineage":1.0,"completed_delta_inversion_composition":0.99,"latest_snapshot_plus_deltas":0.99,"append_oriented_storage":0.97,"storage_experiment_trend":0.95,"xml_only_scope":0.99},"raw_claims":["The system assigns persistent XIDs so that matching XML nodes can retain the same identity in different snapshots.","The XML diff process determines correspondences between nodes in consecutive document versions.","Simple deltas discard information that is needed to reconstruct the previous version.","Completed deltas preserve enough information to support both forward and backward transformation.","Completed deltas can be composed to summarize changes spanning more than one version transition.","The storage architecture can keep the newest XML document together with a sequence of completed deltas for its history.","Installing a new version is designed to require little modification of already stored version objects.","The experiments use simulated changes to study how different version representations affect storage size.","The authors identify compression, temporal querying, and identifier allocation as areas for further work.","Persistent XIDs provide cross-version logical-element lineage, but the paper does not address visual page-region or spreadsheet-cell lineage."],"source_url":"https://www.vldb.org/conf/2001/P581.pdf","access":"full_text"}],"skipped":[]}
